code.text: Bright red blood with most bowel movements for about three months, stools narrower than before, urgency and a feeling of not having finished; more tired than usual on the course since the end of last season
A walk-in clinic put the bleeding down to hemorrhoids two months ago and gave her a cream; she is 41, below the age at which screening starts, and was not examined
She wants to keep competing, and wants to know at once whether whatever this is will mean a colostomy
No known allergy

medicationCodeableConcept.text: Ferrous sulfate 325 mg (65 mg elemental iron) oral tablet, one tablet by mouth every other morning
Dostarlimab-gxly 50 mg/mL injection, 500 mg intravenously over 30 minutes every 3 weeks, for nine doses (six months)

dosageInstruction.text: 500 mg every 3 weeks for nine doses

medicationCodeableConcept.text: Levothyroxine 75 microgram oral tablet, one tablet by mouth each morning on an empty stomach, four hours apart from iron

code.text: Colonoscopy to the cecum with biopsy, under sedation: an ulcerated, friable mass on the posterior and left lateral wall of the lower rectum, about half the circumference, from 4 to 9 cm from the anal verge, not obstructing; six biopsies; the rest of the colon normal; no polyps. Pathology: invasive adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated; immunohistochemistry shows loss of MSH2 and MSH6 with MLH1 and PMS2 retained; microsatellite instability high by PCR

Rectal-protocol MRI of the pelvis (high-resolution T2 and diffusion-weighted): low rectal tumor, lower edge 4 cm from the anal verge and about 1 cm above the anorectal junction, posterior and left lateral, extending 4 mm beyond the muscularis propria (cT3b); two mesorectal lymph nodes of 7 mm with irregular borders (cN1); mesorectal fascia clear by 6 mm; no extramural venous invasion; no lateral pelvic nodes; sphincter complex not involved

coding.display: CT of thorax, abdomen and pelvis with contrast

code.text: CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis with contrast: no liver, lung or peritoneal metastases; no enlarged retroperitoneal nodes

Colorectal multidisciplinary tumor board (medical oncology, colorectal surgery, radiation oncology, radiology, pathology, genetics, wound-ostomy nursing, nurse navigator): mismatch repair-deficient low rectal adenocarcinoma, cT3bN1M0; surgery would most likely need an abdominoperineal resection with a permanent colostomy; recommends PD-1 blockade with dostarlimab for six months, restaging by MRI and endoscopy about every three months, and watch-and-wait if there is a clinical complete response, with chemoradiation and surgery kept in reserve
Chest X-ray, two views: clear lungs, no consolidation, ground-glass change or effusion
Advance care planning conversation, about 20 minutes
Genetic counseling before germline testing: three-generation pedigree as she knows it, consent, and an explanation of what a positive or negative result would mean for her and her blood relatives

Restaging rectal-protocol MRI of the pelvis after four doses: marked regression, with low-signal fibrosis replacing most of the tumor and a small focus of intermediate signal with slight restricted diffusion at the lower margin; mesorectal nodes now 3 mm and smooth; near-complete response
Restaging flexible sigmoidoscopy after four doses: a flat white scar where the tumor was, with a 5 mm shallow ulcer at its lower edge; no mass
Final restaging rectal-protocol MRI of the pelvis after nine doses: low-signal fibrosis only, no intermediate signal and no restricted diffusion; no suspicious lymph nodes; complete response on MRI

code.text: Final restaging CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis with contrast: no metastases
Final restaging flexible sigmoidoscopy after nine doses: a flat white scar with fine surface vessels; no ulcer, nodularity or mass; complete endoscopic response

text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Medical oncology (gastrointestinal) consultation within two weeks, with colorectal surgery, to review the colonoscopy and any biopsy with her and plan staging and treatment if cancer is found
  • Urgent work-up of rectal bleeding with a change in bowel habit and a rectal mass in a woman under 50: colonoscopy with biopsy within days, with mismatch repair testing of any cancer; blood count, ferritin, chemistry and CEA; if cancer is confirmed, rectal-protocol MRI of the pelvis and CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis; return at once for heavy bleeding, fainting or inability to pass stool
  • Oral iron for iron deficiency anemia from blood loss: ferrous sulfate 325 mg on alternate days, a blood count about four weeks after starting, ferritin at about three months, and iron continued for three months after the hemoglobin is normal
  • Germline multigene panel after genetic counseling, because she is under 50 and the tumor is mismatch repair deficient; tumor sequencing for somatic MMR variants if the germline panel is negative; colonoscopy for her first-degree relatives every five years from age 40, or 10 years before the age of her diagnosis if earlier, with Lynch syndrome surveillance only if a germline variant is found
  • Dostarlimab 500 mg intravenously every three weeks for nine doses (six months), with pelvic MRI, flexible sigmoidoscopy and digital rectal examination about every three months; blood count, kidney and liver tests and glucose before each dose and TSH with free T4 every six weeks; teaching about immune-related adverse events with a 24-hour line; hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV screening and a pregnancy test first; contraception continued during treatment and for four months after
  • If the response is incomplete: chemoradiation and total mesorectal excision, as reviewed with the colorectal surgeon, with stoma site marking and teaching by a wound-ostomy nurse before any operation; fertility and sexual function counseling before any pelvic radiation
  • Levothyroxine for immune-related hypothyroidism, with TSH and free T4 six weeks after starting and every six weeks while on PD-1 blockade; dostarlimab continued
  • Watch-and-wait after a clinical complete response: digital rectal examination and flexible sigmoidoscopy every three to four months and pelvic MRI every six months for two years, CEA every three to six months, CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis every six to twelve months, colonoscopy at one year, and a written survivorship care plan; surgery at once for any regrowth
  • Distress and depression screening at each visit; plain explanations with written information; attention to sexual health and body image and to her golf, with an exercise plan she sets; she decides who is told and who receives each note

resource.title: Babe Didrikson Zaharias synthetic care plan
resource.description: Recognize early-onset rectal cancer in a fit woman of 41, below the screening age, whose rectal bleeding and change in bowel habit could be put down to hemorrhoids, and care for it on the NCCN rectal cancer guideline and the ASCO guidance on locally advanced rectal cancer: a digital rectal examination and prompt colonoscopy with biopsy; mismatch repair testing of every colorectal cancer; germline genetic testing because she is under 50; staging by pelvic MRI and CT, with CEA; a multidisciplinary tumor board; and, because the tumor is mismatch repair deficient, PD-1 blockade with dostarlimab and a watch-and-wait strategy after a clinical complete response, sparing her the abdominoperineal resection and permanent colostomy that a tumor this low would otherwise need. The episode also covers immune-related adverse events (hypothyroidism), iron deficiency anemia, sexual health and body image, return to elite sport, screening of first-degree relatives, the USPSTF screening age of 45, and survivorship care, set against her documented operation with a permanent colostomy in 1880 and her return to win a national championship afterwards.
